primarySource.title: Almost 3-Approximate Correlation Clustering in Constant Rounds
inspectedLocations: Introduction: input encoding and objective, printed p. 1
Section 4: r-Pivot-Variant and Claim 4.1, printed pp. 23–24
Section 4: LOCAL implementation / proof of Corollary 1.5, printed pp. 25–26
Appendix B: Lemma B.1, printed pp. 30–31

contract.instance: Unweighted complete signed graph; every unordered vertex pair is positive or negative.
contract.encoding: An ordinary graph G=(V,E) contains exactly the positive pairs; nonedges represent negative pairs.
contract.objective: Number of positive edges crossing clusters plus number of negative pairs inside clusters.
contract.output: A partition into any number of clusters; each vertex learns its own cluster ID.
contract.communicationGraph: The positive-edge graph G itself, not the complete signed graph and not an arbitrary external network.
contract.model: Synchronous LOCAL: one computationally unbounded processor per vertex; communication with neighbors in G.
contract.messageSize: The implementation uses O(log n)-bit messages, so its bandwidth also fits CONGEST.
contract.guaranteeType: Expected objective approximation, not a claimed high-probability approximation ratio.

theorems.sourceLocation: Corollary 1.5, printed p. 4; proof in Section 4, printed pp. 25–26
theorems.statement: For any epsilon > 0, there is a randomized O(1/epsilon)-round LOCAL algorithm for a (3+epsilon)-approximation using O(log n)-bit messages.
theorems.interpretation: Expected approximation; this expectation is explicit in the implementation theorem and follows from Corollary 1.2 / Claim 4.1.
theorems.epsilonScope: The source states any epsilon > 0. A displayed interval such as 0 < epsilon <= 1 would be a plotting restriction, not a theorem restriction.

theorems.equivalentRoundExpression: E[COST] <= (3 + 8/(T-2) + n^{-Omega(1)}) OPT for odd integer T >= 3
theorems.implementation: Each of r Pivot phases uses two communication rounds; one final round assigns clusters.
theorems.randomness: Vertices independently choose ranks uniformly from {0,...,n^c-1}, for sufficiently large constant c, with rank ties broken by vertex ID.
theorems.finiteRankCaution: Do not advertise an exact 3+epsilon guarantee at r=ceil(4/epsilon+1/2) while dropping the rank-collision correction.

theorems.expectedCorrectionUpperBoundFromProof: n^{4-c}, written n^{-Omega(1)} for sufficiently large constant c
theorems.exactZeroOptHandling: If every connected component is a clique, both variants recover the optimum with probability 1. Otherwise OPT >= 1, allowing the collision-event cost to be bounded relative to OPT.
theorems.caution: High probability that ranks are distinct does not turn the expected approximation theorem into a high-probability approximation theorem.

theorems.statement: With a globally uniform random permutation, r-Pivot has expected approximation at most 3+8/(2r-1).
theorems.caveat: The LOCAL implementation uses independently generated finite ranks and therefore includes the additional vanishing correction.

lowerBoundAudit.mainFigureNote: No general LOCAL round lower bound is proved in the supplied source.

excludedClaims.claim: A cited Omega(log n) lower bound for completing parallel greedy MIS / the full Pivot construction.
excludedClaims.reasonExcluded: This is not a round lower bound for all LOCAL correlation-clustering algorithms.

excludedClaims.sourceLocation: Appendix B, Lemma B.1, printed pp. 30–31
excludedClaims.claim: A bad-permutation example for r-Pivot, with claimed cost Omega((n^2/r) OPT) for r<n/2.
excludedClaims.reasonExcluded: Algorithm-specific and permutation-specific; not an expected approximation lower bound and not a universal LOCAL round lower bound.

excludedClaims.claim: Approximation 3 is described as a combinatorial barrier or target.
excludedClaims.reasonExcluded: This is not a proved universal hardness boundary and must not be drawn as a red lower-bound line.

additionalSetupNotMerged.claim: Approximately 2.06+epsilon rounding given a suitable LP solution.
additionalSetupNotMerged.reason: Computing the LP is not included; this is an incompatible extra-input contract, not the same end-to-end LOCAL guarantee.

representationProposal.recommended: Discrete expected-approximation versus elapsed-round tradeoff family.
representationProposal.approximationAxis: Expected approximation upper guarantee; equivalently epsilon above 3.
representationProposal.lowerBoundColor: red reserved for actual verified lower bounds; none supplied here
representationProposal.approximationThreeReference: Neutral reference only, explicitly not a hardness bound.
representationProposal.correctionDisplay: Keep +n^{-Omega(1)} explicit in caption/inspection; if the base curve 3+8/(T-2) is drawn, label it as the main term plus vanishing rank correction.
representationProposal.noNumericSubstitution: Do not assign a numerical exponent to Omega(1) or silently evaluate the correction.
representationProposal.fullAtlas: Retain the green tradeoff and concise labels '(3+epsilon) expected' and 'O(1/epsilon) rounds'; hide theorem detail at distant zoom.
representationProposal.meaningfulClarification: Should the figure show how rounds grow as expected approximation approaches 3, or fix an approximation target such as 3.1?
representationProposal.recommendationReason: A single constant-in-n category hides the only researched tradeoff.
